messages.text:
Great, now prepare two otehr PRs, where you exchange the Si-W EM Calorimeter with the ALLEGRO LAr design. If it needs more space, change the HCAL envelopes accordingly. Also - estimate how much cable, cooling space the LAr based one takes and adapt the HCAL Barrel/EC gaps to host those. 
If LAr can not do the forward part, mark it and we will deal with a dedicated FCAl insertion later.

Call this LAYOUT-002 and put it to the layout mainpage.

I’ll prepare LAYOUT-002 in two PRs: an ALLEGRO-style LAr barrel, then the endcaps and layout-page integration. I’ll check the published dimensions and service needs, adjust the HCAL envelopes, and mark any forward region that needs a later FCal.

The layout main page (#72) has merged. I’ll keep LAYOUT-001 as the Si–W candidate and add LAYOUT-002 alongside it. I’m using the repository’s coordination and design-evidence skills to separate published ALLEGRO facts, nODD adaptations and service-space estimates.

ALLEGRO’s published sampling geometry is larger than the current nODD ECAL slot. I’ll use those dimensions as the reference and retain nODD’s inner 3 T solenoid, treating the coilless LAr cryostat as an adaptation. The readout R&D considers both warm and cold electronics, so I’m estimating their cable and cooling needs separately. [ALLEGRO design paper]([external URL redacted; see source journal])

I’m using the PDF skill to inspect the mechanical and cooling drawings.

The ACTS Spack preflight reports changed setup and lockfile fingerprints. I’ll re-verify the installed DD4hep, Geant4 and datasets before running native geometry checks, using the existing installation.

The service study points to larger gaps: about 0.8 m before the LAr endcap for bends and access, plus 0.5 m behind it for outward routing. I’m also enlarging the rear baths for cold boards and cooling hardware. These are prototype reservations with explicit assumptions, not qualified cable or hydraulic designs.

LAYOUT-002 will show the forward region as uninstrumented and reserved for a later FCal.

The barrel model now includes the inclined absorber plates and both LAr gaps, with explicit channel IDs. I’m checking it in DD4hep and fitting the support rings, electronics and cooling pipes into the reserved space. The endcap implementation is progressing separately; both PRs will document what is physically modelled and what remains a routing reservation.

The complete barrel passes the native geometry checks: 33,792 sensitive LAr volumes, 2.286 million logical cells and no overlaps at 10 nm. The enlarged rear bath fits 16 support rings, 5,888 board slots and 96 cooling branches.

The proposed HCAL front moves to 3.13 m, leaving room for the LAr cryostat and an external service corridor. Cable area and bend-radius estimates fit the reserved gaps, but feedthroughs, connectors and cooling headers still need engineering.

The turbine model retains all three wheels and gives 601,600 logical cells per endcap. Its first active radius is 410 mm; an |η| = 4 ray reaches only about 184–200 mm across the sampling depth. I’m therefore marking that region as uncovered, with empty FCal and forward-collar reservations.

PR #73 is open as a draft for the barrel and shared service study. The second PR will contain the endcaps and the complete LAYOUT-002 overview.

The independent reviews found corrections to the accounting and evidence checks. I’m reconciling the power calculation with the full supply-and-return cable length, treating the published 50 kHz value as a trigger/hit rate, and tightening saved-hit validation to reject nonexistent cells.

The adverse power case exceeds the current cooling allowance. I’ll mark that as an unmet scenario; increasing pipe space alone does not establish cooling capacity.

The first combined barrel-plus-endcap ECAL check found no overlaps, and its 405 material rays show no active LAr coverage at |η| = 4. A review also caught a source-reading error: the quoted endcap absorber thickness includes glue and steel. I’m correcting the lead thickness to match that convention and rerunning the material and transport checks before finalizing the second PR.

The corrected endcaps pass the native material, readout and 10 nm overlap checks. Sparse Geant4 runs also saved valid LAr hits on both endcap orientations. The corrected combined ECAL passes its overlap check and all 405 material rays.

The LAYOUT-002 overview now shows the larger cryostats and HCAL envelopes, the service gaps, and the unbuilt forward insertions alongside LAYOUT-001. I’m closing the records and preparing PR #74.

Both PRs are ready for review: #73 contains the barrel and shared service study; #74 contains the endcaps and the README-linked LAYOUT-002 overview. Merge #73 first, then #74.

The final independent recheck confirmed the lead correction and the retained evidence. I’m checking the GitHub jobs at the final heads before handing them over.

Both PRs are ready, pushed to `asalzburger/nodd`, with CI green:

- [#73 — LAr barrel and service interfaces](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/73)
- [#74 — LAr endcaps and LAYOUT-002 overview](https://github.com/asalzburger/nodd/pull/74), stacked on #73. **Merge #73 first.**

LAYOUT-002 is linked from the README alongside LAYOUT-001. HCAL starts at **3.13 m**, with **800 mm front / 500 mm rear service gaps**. Cable and cooling estimates are documented. **|η| = 4 remains uncovered**, with empty reservations for a later FCal.

Native overlap/material/readout checks and sparse Geant4 tests passed. Adverse cooling scenarios and engineering qualification remain open. No new external software was added.

Token totals remain unchanged; current-session counters were unavailable.
